text:
Christopher Columbus

Frederick’s hand hovered over the vial, the liquid inside shimmering with an unnatural, pearlescent glow. The draft from the hidden chamber had died down, leaving a heavy silence that pressed against his eardrums. He looked at the runes, then at the potion, and finally at the crumbling stone walls of the chamber. He realized that the "eternal life" promised by the ancients was not a gift, but a curse of stagnation—a world where he would watch everyone he loved turn to dust while he remained unchanged, trapped in a loop of memory and grief.

Instead of drinking, Frederick picked up the parchment. He didn't destroy it; he folded it carefully and placed it back into the hollow of the altar. Then, he took the vial of potion and poured it onto the ancient, dry roots of the moss growing in the corner of the chamber. The liquid hissed as it touched the earth, and instantly, vibrant green shoots erupted, blooming into flowers that had not been seen in centuries. The secret to eternal life was not for a man, but for the world that had forgotten how to grow. Frederick left the chamber, closing the stone door behind him, leaving the knowledge buried but the life it contained to flourish in the wild.
